en.intro: Krishna has just said that the wise are confused. Now he names the very problem that traps them, to show Arjuna that he alone has the answer.
en.notice: The verse begins by naming kavayo, the wise, and stating that even they are mohita, deluded. Krishna does not hide the difficulty, but names it fully before offering the way out.
en.next: Krishna now names action, forbidden action, and inaction to show that all three must be understood. Listen closely.
en.meaning: What is action, and what is inaction? Even the wise are confused here. I will explain that action to you, knowing which you will be freed from what is harmful.

hi.intro: कृष्ण ने अभी कहा कि ज्ञानी भी भ्रमित हो जाते हैं। अब वे उस समस्या का नाम लेते हैं जो उन्हें फँसाती है, ताकि अर्जुन समझ सकें कि केवल वे ही इसका उत्तर जानते हैं।
hi.meaning: कर्म क्या है और अकर्म क्या है, इस प्रकार इस विषय में विद्वान् भी मोहित हो जाते हैं। अतः वह कर्म मैं तुम्हें भलीभाँति कहूँगा, जिससे तू अशुभ से मुक्त हो जायगा।
hi.next: कृष्ण अब कर्म, निषिद्ध कर्म और अकर्म का नाम लेते हैं ताकि दिखाया जा सके कि इन तीनों को समझना आवश्यक है। ध्यान से सुनिए।

issues: meaning_changed: "अतः वह कर्मतत्त्व मैं तुम्हें भलीभाँति कहूँगा, जिससे तू अशुभ संसारबन्धन से मुक्त हो जायगा" (The English meaning says 'knowing which you will be freed from what is harmful', but the Hindi translation adds the invented and unsupported word 'कर्मतत्त्व' (the essence of action) and 'संसारबन्धन' (worldly bondage). The original Sanskrit only says 'knowing which you will be freed from the harmful (अशुभात्)', without specifying 'worldly bondage'.)

meaning_changed: "जिससे तू अशुभ से मुक्त हो जायगा" (The Hindi translation drops the crucial word 'कर्म' (action) from 'यत् ज्ञात्वा मोक्ष्यसे' (knowing which [action] you will be freed). It incorrectly implies that merely knowing the answer to the question will free Arjuna, rather than knowing the 'action' (कर्मतत्त्व/कर्म) itself. This changes the meaning from 'knowing the action' to 'knowing this [question/answer]'.)

meaning_changed: "जिससे तू कर्म को जानकर अशुभ से मुक्त हो जायगा" (The Hindi translation adds the word 'कर्म' (action) to the phrase 'जिससे तू... मुक्त हो जायगा', making it mean 'knowing which action you will be freed', whereas the source and English translation state 'knowing which you will be freed' (referring to the explanation/knowledge of action, not the action itself).)

contrast_template: "इस प्रकार इस विषय में" (The Hindi translation uses the word 'इस प्रकार' (thus/in this manner) at the beginning of the first clause, which acts as a contrastive or consequential marker that is not present in the source Sanskrit 'कर्म क्या है और अकर्म क्या है' and alters the direct, interrogative flow of the original text.)
